changes.before: Wrong: It describes the opposite action of cutting services, not providing support.
changes.after: Wrong: Reducing services is not the meaning of allocating resources; the source describes support for longer hours.

changes.before: I will allocate resources to buy a coffee on my way to work.
changes.after: Our club will allocate resources to organizing the weekend workshop.

changes.before: Wrong: Buying a single coffee is too trivial to need formal provision of money, staff, or time.
changes.after: Wrong: The infinitive after to must be organize, not organizing, in this sentence.

changes.before: They allocated resources to enjoy the weekend together.
changes.after: Our club will allocate resources for organize the weekend workshop.

changes.before: Wrong: Enjoying the weekend is general leisure, not a specific purpose needing provision of support.
changes.after: Wrong: After the preposition for, use organizing rather than the bare verb organize.

changes.before: Only b shows providing support for a clear purpose with natural collocation.
changes.after: Option b uses to + base verb correctly; a uses an -ing form after infinitival to, while c uses a bare verb after for.

changes.before: Our team met the deadline and submitted the report three weeks late.
changes.after: Our team meeted the deadline and submitted the report before Friday.

changes.before: Wrong: Submitting three weeks late contradicts finishing by the required time.
changes.after: Wrong: The past tense of meet is met, not meeted.

changes.before: She met the deadline with her friends at the café yesterday.
changes.after: Our team met deadline and submitted the report before Friday.

changes.before: Wrong: It confuses meeting people with the idiom for finishing by the required time.
changes.after: Wrong: The singular count noun deadline needs a determiner here; use met the deadline.

changes.before: Only a shows finishing on time with correct grammar and meaning.
changes.after: Option a uses met and the required determiner; b has the wrong past tense, and c omits the determiner.
